Header: Pseudomonas syringae pv. tabaci (Tox-) Chiwawu chakuda

Prevention: Rotate nursery sites and fields every 3 to 4 years with the following non-host crops such as groundnuts and maize.
Keep nursery and fields weed free to prevent alternative hosts from harbouring the pathogen inoculum.
Fumigate seedbeds - See yellow direct control column
Uproot and burn all infected plants soon after complete reaping tobacco to prevent spread of pathogen
There are currently no resistant varieties of tobacco against this disease
Avoid overhead irrigation as this can spread the bacterium
Monitoring: Check for brown to black angular leaf spot(s) with irregular shapes (as they are limited by the leaf veins) from 2 weeks after planting
When spots merge together they can form large dead areas.
The centre of the large area may fall out giving the leaves a ragged appearance
Diseased leaves become necrotic and dry
Monitor every 3 days in wet and humid weather as the disease is much worse in these conditions
Control should be carried out as soon as disease symptoms are noticed
Direct Control: Uproot and burn all infected plants soon after complete reaping tobacco to kill the pathogen
Reap from clean area with infected portions to avoid disease spread
Reap all mature infected leaves to prevent spread of disease and burn
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
Spray copper oxychloride (any trade name) from 4 weeks after sowing at the rate of 20g/10 litres of water.
Repeat application every 2 weeks after initial application in hot spot disease areas.
WG) at the rate of 60g/ha in 400 litres of water (in the field).
Apply 4 weeks after planting and repeat two weeks later.
